subject: Request: carveout for streaming token emission expectations (TTFT & sustained tokens/sec)
messages:
From: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@stellardata.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@stellardata.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on streaming vs sync SLA commitments for POC

Hi Grace,

Quick follow up from our technical review: the POC is showing good quality but our compliance and SRE teams are nervous about how streaming endpoints are called out in the draft SOW. Specifically they're looking for firm language around:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming calls vs non-streaming responses
- Sustained token/sec guarantees (or approved ranges) for high-throughput streaming workloads

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a carveout or an exception path for the POC (30-day pilot) where we accept a looser TTFT for streaming but have a guaranteed minimum sustained token throughput for a 95th percentile window?

If possible, please send a short amendment we can share with legal. We need this to move the PO and the security review forward.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Baxter
Head of Integrations — Stellar Data Inc.

Attachment: sample-call-trace.json (json)
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@stellardata.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, contracts@stellardata.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming vs sync SLA commitments for POC

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Appreciate the call traces you sent. Short answers up front, details & proposed amendment below.

Summary:
- We can offer a scoped exception for the 30-day pilot that separates TTFT guarantees (streaming) from sustained throughput guarantees.
- Proposed: no hard TTFT SLA for streaming (we guarantee best-effort optimized TTFT; typical median ~80–120ms on our hosted tier), but we will commit to a sustained token emission floor of 250 tokens/sec at the 95th percentile for any single request stream during the pilot, subject to request size limits and concurrency caps documented below.

Key constraints and operational controls:
- Applies only to the pilot bundle (deal SL-2027-0421) and the specific model family listed in Appendix A of the amendment.
- Sustained token/sec commitment is measured per active stream over a 60s sliding window (95th percentile).
- If we hit capacity limits that threaten the commitment, automatic fallback to a compatible non-streaming variant with a 99.9% availability SLA will be used; Redwood will notify and provide logs.
- Concurrency cap: 40 concurrent streaming sessions per customer allocation in the pilot. Above that, bursts are best-effort and not covered by the commitment.

Next steps: I’m attaching a draft amendment (redwood-amendment-draft-v1.pdf) that legal can review. Aditya / Karthik — please confirm the measurement definition (60s window / 95th percentile) and the operational fallback language works for engineering.

Action items for Tom:
- Confirm that Stellar accepts the 250 tokens/sec floor and the 40-session concurrency cap for the pilot, or propose alternate numbers.
- If agreed, Legal can route the amendment and we’ll fast-track the pilot SLA change.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood-amendment-draft-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming vs sync SLA commitments for POC

Looping in the runtime and product side. Quick technical clarifications:

- Measurement: 250 tokens/sec per stream (95th percentile over a 60s sliding window) is workable for our hosted testband with the current kernel scheduling, assuming quantized model variants are used for the pilot. We should call out sequence-length limits (e.g., streams >2048 context need special handling).
- TTFT: we can’t provide a binding TTFT SLA for streaming across global regions due to routing variability; we can provide a regional median and a best-effort guardrail.
- Fallback behavior: automated routing to non-streaming variant will preserve response completeness, but it may increase latency to final response. We will include telemetry IDs for traceability.

I propose adding a short table in Appendix B of the amendment with:
- model variant, quantization level, per-stream token/sec floor, per-stream max sequence length, concurrency cap, measurement window.

Lauren — legal will want explicit rollback/termination triggers if we repeatedly miss the sustained token/sec floor. Suggest 3 strike windows within the pilot.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Inference Runtime
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: contracts@stellardata.com
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@stellardata.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for streaming token emission expectations (TTFT & sustained tokens/sec)

Hi Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround and the amendment. Stellar Legal is OK with the carveout in principle but has two edits:

1) Replace the 60s sliding window measurement with a clarified sampling approach (sampled 10s sub-windows aggregated to a 60s reporting window) and require transparent telemetry exports to Stellar’s SRE for any window where the commitment is missed.
2) Add a clause that allows Stellar to request a temporary traffic-shift test (1 hour) to validate sustained throughput on the dedicated pilot allocation; Redwood to provide a point-of-contact and short escalation SLA for that test.

We can accept the 250 tokens/sec floor but would like the concurrency cap raised to 60 for the pilot. If Redwood agrees to the sampling refinement and the test clause, we'll route the amendment for signature.

We’ve attached a redline (slo-exception-mpa-stellardata.docx) with the edits. Please advise.

Regards,
Contracts — Stellar Data Inc.
contracts@stellardata.com
